To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
atomically clean, oxygen-free, stoichiometric AIN(000 1) surfaces can be produced in situ by exposing the (0001)-oriented surface of AlN films to flowing NH3 at high temperatures and low pressures.

the (0001)-oriented surfaces of AlN films can be prepared in situ by exposure to flowing ammonia at high temperatures and that this process leaves the surface structure and surface microstructure unchanged.

high-temperature exposure of the (1×3) reconstructed (0001) surfaces of AlN thin film to flowing NH3 at 1120°C and 10–4Torr for 30 min removes oxygen/hydroxide and hydrocarbons below the detection limits of XPS and decreases the Al/N ratio from 1 to 1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel method to prepare atomically clean, high-quality stoichiometric surfaces on the (0001)-oriented surfaces of AlN thin-film samples.
the development of a surface preparation procedure that produces a stoichiometric, atomically clean surface of AlN.
the characterization of atomically cleaned surfaces of AIN thin films, and it provides a foundation for future studies of the surface reactivity of AlN.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the (0001)-oriented surface of AlN is not chemically stable at 1120±10 °C under a flowing NH3 gas at 10−4 Torr and at 1175±10 °C at 10−7 Torr.
the (0001)-oriented surfaces of AlN thin film samples can be made atomically clean and stoichiometric by high-temperature exposure of the samples to flowing ammonia.
a stoichiometric, atomically clean AlN surface is obtained by high temperature (∼1000 °C) exposure to flowing ammonia gas in a UHV environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface chemistry of AlN(0001) is similar to that of Al(111), except for the fact that AlN(000)1 is stable in air at 25 °C, whereas Al(111) is unstable at room temperature.
the (0001)-oriented surface of AlN is stable to high-temperature exposure at low pressure in the presence of NH3 and that the (000-1)-oriented surface is stable in vacuum at high temperature.

the (0001)-oriented surfaces of AlN thin film samples can be cleaned by exposure to flowing NH3 at high temperatures and low pressures, and this treatment leaves the surfaces with the same stoichiometry, surface structure, and microstructure as observed for the as-loaded surfaces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the (0001)-oriented AlN surfaces can be cleaned in a high-temperature, ammonia-containing environment without changing the surface structure and the surface roughness.
the (0001)-oriented surfaces of AlN thin film samples can be prepared with the Al∕Ni atomic ratios of 1.0, which are close to the stoichiometric value of 1.
it is not necessary to use a high-temperature, high-pressure, or high-flux ammonia source to clean the surface of AlN.
